papers.title: Big Secrets Small Shares: Revisiting Secure Multi-Party Computation
papers.abstract: At CRYPTO 2007, Damg{\aa}rd and Nielsen introduced a preprocessing approach to multi-party computation (MPC) to achieve linear communication complexity. Another approach to reduce communication complexity was proposed by Cramer, Damg{\aa}rd, and de Haan at EUROCRYPT 2007, which involved using ramp-secret sharing schemes to jointly share base-field components of secrets from the extension field. In this paper, we combine these two ideas to achieve a non-asymptotic reduction of communication cost in a multi-phase MPC setup. We introduce a new modification of the ramp secret sharing scheme, called compact sharing, and tailor the MPC protocol to accommodate this modification. Compact sharing masks the polynomial coefficients that would otherwise leak during degree reduction. The protocol provides perfect security against static semi-honest adversaries under an explicit tradeoff between the corruption threshold and the extension degree. When the extension degree scales linearly with the number of parties, the gate-evaluation core achieves constant communication overhead relative to an extension-field element, amortized over full preprocessing batches; input and output communication is counted separately.

papers.title: Claims of emergence in AI should be grounded in information decomposition
papers.abstract: When a language model develops capabilities not traceable to its individual components, when a multi-agent AI system outperforms each agent on its own, or when a human-AI pair succeeds where either fails in isolation, AI researchers describe it as a case of ``synergy'' or ``emergence''. However, these are usually informal assessments not supported by a theoretical framework, making these claims impossible to compare or even meaningfully dispute. Here we argue that \emph{information decomposition can serve as a unifying formal framework to operationalize assessments about synergy in AI systems}. Information decomposition provides a way to distinguish qualitatively different \emph{types} of information, including unique information available from individual components, redundant information shared across multiple components, and synergistic information accessible only from parts taken together. This gives claims of emergence a precise, falsifiable criterion: a system's behavior is emergent only if it carries synergistic information about task-relevant outcomes. We apply this lens to attention heads, autonomous agents, and human-AI teams, showing how it organizes existing knowledge across scales and substrates, while also generating cross-level conjectures that siloed fields would miss.

papers.title: On the hardness of approximating minimum distances of quantum codes
papers.abstract: The problem of computing distances of error-correcting codes is fundamental in both the classical and quantum settings. While hardness for the classical version of these problems has been known for some time (in both the exact and approximate settings), it was only recently that Kapshikar and Kundu showed the hardness of these problems for non-degenerate quantum codes. As our first main result, we get a direct reduction to CSS codes, the most commonly used type of quantum code, from the minimum distance problem for classical linear codes. In particular, our proof uses arguably simpler constructions based on hypergraph product codes. Our second set of results considers the distance of a graph state, which is a key parameter for quantum codes obtained via the codeword stabilized formalism. We show that it is NP-hard to compute/approximate the distance of a graph state, which is a degenerate quantum code, when the adjacency matrix of the graph is the input. This establishes hardness for even degenerate quantum codes, which was not known before. Furthermore, we show this is true even if we only consider X-type errors of a graph state. Our techniques, moreover, imply an interesting classical consequence: the hardness of computing or approximating the distance of classical codes with rate equal to 1/2. One of the main motivations of the present work is a question raised by Kapshikar and Kundu concerning the NP-hardness of approximation when there is an additive error proportional to a quantum code's length. We show that no such hardness can hold for hypergraph product codes. These observations suggest the possibility of a new kind of square root barrier.

papers.title: Serial Depth of Adaptive Parallel Sampling: Lower Bounds and Schedules for Masked Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models generate sequences in rounds, predicting several masked positions at once. Fewer rounds can accelerate decoding, but sampling positions independently can lose their dependence and bias the output. How few rounds suffice for a prescribed error budget? Beyond error bounds for individual decoding rules, we study sharp lower bounds on the number of rounds required for a given target distribution. We introduce serial depth: the minimum number of rounds, averaged over target sequences, needed to meet a forward Kullback-Leibler error budget. With exact conditional probabilities, we prove these bounds for all deterministic rules that may adapt to generated values and construct matching schedules for several distribution families, with depths ranging from $\log\log n$ to linear in sequence length $n$. To narrow the gap to trained models, we show that these lower bounds remain valid for learned predictors and give sufficient accuracy conditions on visited contexts for schedules to retain their error guarantees. On two pretrained models across five text domains, a schedule suggested by the theory achieves higher average log-likelihood on held-out text in five rounds than random selection in eight. A preregistered confirmation study certifies a relative improvement on independent dialogue data.

papers.title: Birthday Estimators Are Uniformly Optimal for Renyi Entropy
papers.abstract: Collisions are a basic probe of unknown distributions, used for testing and for counting substructures in graphs, and they underlie R\'enyi entropy, a fundamental measure of uncertainty with applications in cryptography, machine learning, physics, and biology. Motivated by this, we study the natural birthday estimator. We prove Bernstein-type concentration for it and show that it is minimax optimal, uniformly and jointly in alphabet size, order, accuracy, and confidence, with no sample splitting, clipping, or median aggregation. This, in particular, settles the sample complexity of integer-order R\'enyi entropy estimation up to absolute constants in all regimes, closing the gap between the best known upper and lower bounds. Our concentration bound rests on a sensitivity analysis of collision count, and the matching lower bound on a sharp analysis of detecting a hidden spike in a plateau distribution.

papers.title: Moment Ambiguity and the Limits of Robust Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We study fundamental information-theoretic limits of robust stochastic optimization when the distribution is known only through its exact moment sequence. We develop a unified framework that produces families of distinct distributions sharing all moments yet inducing radically different optimal decisions, thereby establishing strong impossibility results for a range of decision problems under moment ambiguity. Our binary and $N$-way moment-matching constructions separate quantiles, threshold regions, and online selection opportunities while preserving every moment. For the newsvendor problem, moment equivalence causes quantile ambiguity, inducing any fixed or randomized order quantity to fail arbitrarily badly. For revenue maximization, no deterministic or randomized posted pricing scheme can secure a nontrivial approximation relative to the full-information benchmark. For the secretary problem with cardinal observations, the optimal robust success probability under exact moment disclosure is the classical finite-horizon value $s_m$, even for i.i.d. observations. This value converges to $1/e$, compared with the full-information limit of approximately $0.5801$ due to Gilbert and Mosteller (J. Am. Stat. Assoc., 1966). We also recover and expand upon the recent impossibility result of Correa et al. (STOC, 2026) for prophet inequalities with moment knowledge. For every fixed $r\ge1$, exact moment knowledge can yield at best a $\Theta(1/\log m)$ competitive ratio, even when competing against relaxed benchmarks based on expected $r$-th order statistics or when the algorithm is allowed to select $r$ items.

papers.title: CorteXforge: Scenario-Based RF Dataset Generation on Real Testbeds
papers.abstract: Deep learning for radio frequency (RF) signal analysis relies on large annotated datasets, yet synthetic datasets trade physical realism for controllability, while uncontrolled over-theair measurements offer realism but limited reproducibility. We present CorteXforge, a scenario-based framework for generating realistic and reproducible RF datasets on programmable software defined radio (SDR) testbeds. High-level RF scenarios are automatically translated into synchronized experiments executed on the SLICES-RI/CorteXlab platform, producing fully annotated Signal Metadata Format (SIGMF) datasets that capture hardware impairments and propagation effects. We validate CorteXforge through automatic modulation classification using ModForge, an over-the-air (OTA) dataset generated with the framework. Cross-domain experiments reveal a synthetic-to-real performance gap and show that synthetic pretraining remains beneficial for adaptation to OTA data. CorteXforge provides a practical foundation for reproducible RF dataset generation and future research on domain generalization.

papers.title: Hilbert-Scale Stability of Posterior Diffusion Priors for Ill-Posed Signal Recovery
papers.abstract: Indirect and noisy observations are difficult to invert when the forward operator smooths out the unknown signal. In this case, the unstable modes are precisely the modes that the data reveals least, thus the success of any reconstruction method depends on how prior information interacts with the geometry of the operator across regularity scales. Diffusion priors have become ubiquitous for such problems; however, the current theory still does not determine when a learned score remains informative under ill-posed forward operators. In this paper, we study posterior diffusion for linear inverse problems on Hilbert scales and derive a stability theory under an explicit score-amplification condition. Under a smoothing condition on the forward map, a source condition on the truth, and weak-norm control of score error, we derive non-asymptotic recovery bounds in \(\Hs^s\) that separate observation noise, score approximation, and reverse-time discretization. These bounds give a recoverable regularity threshold determined jointly by operator smoothing, truth regularity, score regularity, and the posterior correction. The threshold specifies the Hilbert-scale norms \(\Hs^s\) in which weak-norm score error remains controlled after propagation through the posterior reverse dynamics. For larger regularity indices \(s\), the inverse geometry magnifies the same error, and the Hilbert-scale recovery estimate no longer gives uniform stability. We also prove that a posterior correction adapted to the forward operator improves stability relative to isotropic guidance in the regularity ranges where the smoothing action of the forward map matters most. The recovery estimates give a regularity-sensitive theory of posterior diffusion and show how learned score error, operator smoothing, and reconstruction norm jointly determine the stable range predicted by the analysis.

papers.title: Sionna Bench: Towards Benchmarks in Wireless Communications
papers.abstract: Academic research in wireless communications has no tradition of benchmarks so far. Remarkable progress in benchmark-oriented fields like machine learning suggests that the adoption of benchmarks could benefit our field. In the absence of benchmarks, however, a scientific debt has accumulated: since the academic community has not canonized specific problem setups, methods that address essentially the same problem were often developed for slightly different setups and lack a common framework for comparison. Any attempt to establish a new benchmark is faced with the challenge of resolving this debt. Recent advances in agentic artificial intelligence (AI) create an opportunity to do so by leveraging AI-assisted coding. This makes it possible to implement the state-of-the art at scale and to adapt it to a common framework for comparison. We present Sionna Bench to initiate benchmarks in academic wireless communications research. As a pilot study, we use the problem of MIMO-OFDM channel estimation. At the time of writing, Sionna Bench's channel estimation benchmark features twenty channel estimation methods that were implemented from ten different papers. The ability to compare methods against the state-of-the-art will be crucial for navigating the research landscape in an era where AI-generated methods coexist with human-developed algorithms.

papers.title: AoI-Aware Polar Code Blind Rate Adaptation
papers.abstract: We study adaptive prefix-length selection for reliability-ordered coded transmission over $N$ coordinates, using only the $K$ most reliable, to balance age of information (AoI) against throughput. An additive-increase/decrease (AID) prefix-walk controller updates the prefix length from the last decoding outcome alone, at $O(1)$ per-slot cost with no channel estimation, inducing an irreducible birth--death chain whose mean drift fixes a unique balance point $K^\dagger$ (largest $K$ with success probability $\ge\tfrac12$), around which the stationary distribution concentrates geometrically. We derive this distribution in closed form via detailed balance and obtain exact steady-state AoI and goodput via renewal-reward analysis. Simulations on a $64$-coordinate polar code over a binary symmetric channel (BSC) confirm these predictions to within $0.3\%$. Relative to a genie-aided upper bound with perfect channel knowledge, we further quantify the goodput cost of adapting from a single feedback bit alone.

papers.title: Information, Estimation, and Prediction for Discrete Memoryless Channels via Poissonization
papers.abstract: We develop information--estimation relations for an arbitrary discrete memoryless channel with finite input and output alphabets by varying the expected number of observations while keeping the channel fixed. A single hidden input is observed through a Poisson number of conditionally independent channel uses, whose mean specifies the observation budget. The derivative of mutual information with respect to this budget equals the minimum expected relative-entropy loss for estimating the input's output distribution. The posterior average of the channel's output distributions achieves this minimum and is the Bayesian predictor for the next observation. When the input distribution, the channel, or both are misspecified, the relative entropy between the true and assumed observation laws is the integral of the excess prediction loss over the budget. We also extend these relations to finite-state processes taking values in the input alphabet and observed through the channel at independent Poisson sampling times. Both in the matched setting and under model mismatch, the expected prediction loss accumulated over time using past observations equals the corresponding loss using the full observation record (noncausal estimation), averaged over lower sampling rates.

papers.title: Efficient Perturbation-Based SC Decoding for Long Polar Codes
papers.abstract: Soft information perturbations can significantly improve the successive cancellation (SC) decoding performance of polar codes. This is an effective method for realizing low-latency yet high performance for long polar codes, since each perturbation-based SC (PSC) decoding can be performed in parallel. However, little theoretical insight has been revealed so far regarding its work rationale. This paper provides the theoretical analysis of the soft information perturbation. It reveals that PSC decoding improves the SC decoding performance through correcting the erroneous bit estimations, especially the first erroneous bit (FEB). It further validates that perturbing the soft information does not degrade the error-correction capability of SC decoding. Such revelations lead to the design of optimal perturbations that maximizes the FEB correction probability, resulting in an enhanced PSC decoding performance. Based on this, a novel hybrid PSC (HPSC) decoding is proposed. By introducing the random and biased perturbations, the HPSC decoding can better divert from the initial erroneous estimation and converge to the intended one. Our simulation results demonstrate that with the optimal perturbation, the HPSC decoding can achieve a similar performance as the cyclic redundancy check (CRC) aided SC list (CA-SCL) decoding, while avoiding path sorting and expansion.

papers.title: Certified Adaptive List Decoding for Error-Correcting Codes
papers.abstract: Maximum-likelihood (ML) decoding of linear block codes is NP-hard, so neural decoders are evaluated by how closely they approach it. We observe that proving a candidate optimal can be far easier than finding it, and build a decoder that does both. We cast decoding as a search over an absorbing-state discrete diffusion model, whose sequential commitment of coordinates turns generation into a tree, and run a probability beam search over it. A dual bound from a linear-programming relaxation and a distance-based test, both derived from the code, then certify per frame that the current candidate is the global ML solution; because both are theorems, certified frames incur no accuracy-computation trade-off. Across $15$ codes and five operating points we certify up to $99.9\%$ of frames, the two tests dividing the space as their derivations predict, one strong for sparse parity-check matrices and the other for codes with a large minimum distance. Certification also behaves as a per-frame reliability signal, with $96.7$-$100\%$ of all frame errors falling on uncertified frames. Against an exact ML reference at $5$ dB the decoder is within one standard deviation on three of the four codes where the reference is uncensored, and against four neural baselines it attains the best bit-error rate in $71$ of $75$ cells.

papers.title: infomeasure-rs: A High-Performance Rust Library for Information-Theoretic Measures and Estimators
papers.abstract: Information theory has become a standard tool across the natural and social sciences, yet practical use is limited by estimator choice, fragmented software, reproducibility, and computational cost. We present infomeasure-rs, an open-source Rust library that brings a broad set of information-theoretic measures and estimators into one self-contained, type-safe package. It covers entropy, mutual information, conditional mutual information, transfer entropy, conditional transfer entropy, cross-entropy, and the Kullback-Leibler and Jensen-Shannon divergences, with discrete (plug-in and bias-corrected), kernel, ordinal, and nearest-neighbour estimators, including the R\'enyi and Tsallis families, and exposes local and global values and significance testing through a consistent trait interface. It ships as a single portable binary with no runtime dependency and is continuously validated against a reference implementation. On a single central processing unit (CPU) core, and even without its GPU or parallel paths, it is the fastest of the packages we compared across languages, matching the closest packages only for plug-in discrete entropy and substantially faster for mutual information, the conditional and transfer measures, and the kernel, ordinal, and generalised-entropy estimators. The optional GPU and multi-threaded paths accelerate selected continuous estimators further. The library is open source and, to our knowledge, the most complete information-theory package for Rust.

papers.title: Error-correction Decoding for 2D Convolutional Codes with a Generalized Viterbi Algorithm
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) convolutional codes are a generalization of one-dimensional (1D) convolutional codes and are naturally suitable for encoding two-dimensional data. Although their theoretical properties are well established, practical applications are limited due to the lack of error-correction decoding algorithms. While the Viterbi algorithm provides an efficient decoding method for 1D convolutional codes, no analogous approach exists for the 2D case. In this paper, we introduce a decoding algorithm for 2D convolutional codes, called the 2D Viterbi algorithm, extending the principles of the classical Viterbi algorithm to the two-dimensional setting. The presented 2D Viterbi algorithm works with linear systems representations of 2D convolutional codes and its complexity depends on the dimension of the corresponding 2D linear system. Hence, we also provide several algorithms to obtain 2D realizations of small dimension.

papers.title: Certified Non-Degenerate Maximum-Likelihood Benchmarking of Quantum LDPC Decoders
papers.abstract: The measured logical error rate of a quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) code depends on the decoding algorithm. We develop a framework that certifies non-degenerate maximum-likelihood (ML) decoding outcomes on individual sampled shots under circuit-level noise, providing a common reference for comparing decoders and codes. Upper and lower bounds on the minimum correction cost in the true and competing logical classes establish success, failure, or an undecided outcome. Branch-and-bound search refines these intervals while retaining valid bounds under resource limits. Counting the outcomes bounds the empirical ML logical error rate, with interval width equal to the undecided fraction. Results for two bivariate bicycle codes show that best-first ordered statistics decoding (BF-OSD) tracks the non-degenerate ML benchmark closely while leaving some ML-correctable shots.

papers.title: Length Bounds for Irreducible Cyclic MDS Codes
papers.abstract: We prove the MDS length bound for nontrivial irreducible cyclic codes of every composite length. The classical trace realization turns the MDS property into independence of elements of a multiplicative subgroup. Every nonidentity subgroup must have the full extension degree. This restriction yields length congruences, and the Frobenius-orbit description of the coefficient field gives an exact descent obstruction. A cyclotomic argument reduces each fixed dimension to finitely many parameters. For dimensions at most thirty, established geometric bounds reduce the alphabet to a small finite range; the remaining twelve parameter triples are excluded by explicit products of at most three determinant factors and a low-degree multiplier argument. An independent argument proves the composite-length theorem in arbitrary dimension. The standardness conclusion is stated separately as a conditional consequence of the classification statement of Feng, Hollmann, Li, and Xiang; the correct extension-field reduction retains a semilinear quotient. The general prime-length problem is not settled here. Neither length proof uses the automorphism classification or the recent odd-characteristic range announced by Fan.

papers.title: Lower bounds for Bayesian CVaR in interactive problems with local differential privacy
papers.abstract: We develop an information-theoretic method for lower bounding the prior-predictive conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of loss in interactive statistical decision making (ISDM). A generalized Fano inequality replaces a single error event by a randomized binary statistic constructed from a bounded transform of the loss, reducing the problem to a Bernoulli $f$-divergence inequality. A bounded hinge transform yields a direct lower bound on Bayesian CVaR under a prior fixed in advance. We derive reverse-KL specializations and obtain explicit bounds for Gaussian mean estimation and Gaussian stochastic bandits. We then impose local differential privacy (LDP) at the observation stage of the same ISDM model. LDP contraction inequalities combined with the adaptive KL chain rule give explicit Bayesian CVaR lower bounds for Gaussian mean estimation with heterogeneous privacy parameters and Gaussian $K$-armed bandits.

papers.title: Worst-Case Bayesian CVaR Regret Bounds for Episodic Markov Decision Processes
papers.abstract: We study the worst-case, over priors, Bayesian conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) of cumulative pseudo-regret in time-homogeneous finite-horizon episodic Markov decision processes. A high-probability guarantee for UCBVI-BF yields a prior-predictive upper bound. A lower bound follows by a three-state MDP and applying a reverse-KL inequality. For a constant number of states, the bounds have the same polynomial dependence on horizon, actions, and episodes, with a logarithmic gap in the risk level.

papers.title: Exact Storage-Repair-Bandwidth Tradeoffs for $(6,5,5)$ and $(7,6,6)$ Exact-Repair Regenerating Codes
papers.abstract: This note provides exact information-theoretic outer bounds that completely characterize the storage-repair-bandwidth tradeoff regions for the cases $(n,k,d)=(6,5,5)$ and $(7,6,6)$. The layered code proposed by Tian et al. achieves the tradeoff and is thus optimal. GPT-6 Astra assisted in the discovery of these bounds, based on a new conditioning argument and a structured search over the restricted subsets of entropy linear program constraints. The proofs are given as exact integer-valued certificates, which are difficult for direct human verification, and a Python verifier is included as part of the package, together with the certificates.

papers.title: Nonequivalence of $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear and $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear generalized Hadamard codes for odd primes
papers.abstract: The $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-additive codes are subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\alpha_1}\times\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}^{\alpha_2}$, and they can be seen as linear codes over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ when $\alpha_2=0$, as $\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-additive codes when $\alpha_1=0$, and as $\mathbb{Z}_2\mathbb{Z}_4$-additive codes when $p=2$. A $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear generalized Hadamard (GH) code is a GH code over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ which is the Gray map image of a $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-additive code. For every prime $p$, there are recursive constructions of $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear GH codes $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ with $\alpha_1\neq0$ and $\alpha_2\neq0$, and of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear GH codes $\bar H_p^{t_1,\dots,t_s}$. We show that the kernel blocks of a nonlinear code $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ give equivalent punctured codes, and that these punctured codes are linear. Any of them is called the derived code of $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$. We also determine the ranks of the codes $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ and $\bar H_p^{t_1,t_2}$. For odd $p$, the rank of $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ depends on the Bernoulli numbers modulo $p$. By comparing the derived codes and the ranks, we show that, for odd $p$, no code $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ is equivalent to any of these $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear GH codes. For $p=2$, a nonlinear code $H_2^{t_1,t_2}$ is equivalent to a $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-linear Hadamard code if and only if $t_2\geq2$. Finally, we count the nonequivalent codes in the union of both families.

papers.title: Generative Diffusion Models for Secure UAV-ISAC with Real-Time Target Tracking
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms with integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) are prime candidates for surveillance missions, in which a dual-function drone tracks a mobile target and alerts a ground station when the target enters a protected region. Such alerts generate event-triggered communication traffic. By observing the change in the traffic, an eavesdropper (Eve) can therefore learn in real time whether the target is detected inside the protected region without decoding any message. Existing physical-layer security techniques protect the message content or hide that a transmission occurs, but the composition of the traffic remains exposed. We formulate the threat as traffic-composition covertness and propose a keyless diffusion-based transmission scheme that hides the triggered traffic. The scheme superposes the beamformed information streams of the UAV with a message-agnostic safeguard waveform generated by a conditional denoising diffusion implicit model. Training shapes the safeguard distribution such that triggered and non-triggered slots become statistically indistinguishable at Eve. The legitimate user shares no secret key with the UAV. We formulate the joint design as a rate maximization under covertness, reliability, and sensing constraints, with the sensing accuracy measured by the posterior Cram\'er-Rao bound (PCRB) of the beam-dependent tracking problem. Our numerical results show that, with multiple transmit antennas and an Eve signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $5$~dB, a learned Eve stays near the blind guess of $0.5$ for every safeguard beam split, a detector that knows the safeguard model reaches $0.71$ to $0.73$ inside Bob's main lobe and $0.53$ to $0.55$ outside it, while the average position PCRB varies only between $0.59$ and $0.70$~m$^2$.

papers.title: Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Switch Networks: Memory Limits and Achievability
papers.abstract: We study the minimum persistent memory required to distribute a graph state through a quantum switch. Specifically, consider a central switch that assists $n$ remote users in distributing a graph state, using independently generated user-switch Bell pairs. Since Bell-pair generation is probabilistic, different links generally succeed at different times. When a Bell-pair is generated, the qubits may need to be stored in memory while waiting for other links to succeed. Recently, new protocols have been proposed to reduce this storage overhead by processing and releasing some switch qubits before all Bell links are available. However, these protocols do not characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required at each stage. Moreover, the local-cover method in the state-of-the-art Piecemaker protocol is computationally expensive for general target graphs. In this work, we characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required after any subset of users' Bell links are generated and processed. We then develop an online stabilizer-transition protocol that attains this limit, which can be implemented in polynomial time in the number of qubits $n$. Remarkably, this optimal protocol can provide substantial memory reductions over existing heuristic approaches. In particular, for the path graph $P_n$ over $n$ users, Piecemaker protocol requires at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ qubits of peak persistent memory for \textit{every Bell-links generation order}, whereas under the order $(1,2,\ldots,n)$, our protocol requires only one persistent switch qubit. Finally, the same stabilizer-transition framework also provides a direct forward construction for sequential graph-state generation using the minimum number of quantum emitters, equal to the maximum of the height function.

papers.title: Robust Latent Variable Graphical Models: Exact Recovery and Fundamental Limits
papers.abstract: We study robust estimation of a Gaussian precision matrix that decomposes as a sparse matrix minus a symmetric, possibly indefinite, low-rank matrix, a structure that arises when latent-variable marginalization is combined with conditioning on linear measurements. The proposed convex estimator replaces the sample covariance by the centered Gaussian measure-transformed (MT) covariance, which preserves the signed graph of the sparse component under the nominal model, and penalizes the low-rank component by the nuclear norm of a congruence transform, an atomic norm that encodes structural side information. Our main result is a primal--dual witness theorem: under restricted invertibility and irrepresentability conditions on the Fisher information, the raw convex optimizer is unique, has no false edges, recovers the signs of all sufficiently strong edges, and has exactly the true rank and inertia. These conditions reduce to the graphical-lasso conditions when the low-rank part is absent, and we verify them from primitive incoherence and near-isotropy assumptions. Over a class on which they hold uniformly, we prove information-theoretic limits for Frobenius estimation, signed graph recovery, and inertia recovery. In particular, inertia recovery requires $N\gtrsim p/\nu_{\min}^2$ samples, where $\nu_{\min}$ is the smallest nonzero eigenvalue modulus of the low-rank part; the spectral beta-min condition of the witness theorem is necessary up to a $\sqrt{\log p}$ factor; and the Frobenius risk attains the minimax rate up to a factor $\sqrt{\mu(1+\min\{d,r\})\log p}$, where $\mu$ is the incoherence parameter, $d$ the maximal degree, and $r$ the rank. We further quantify robustness under Huber contamination, with a bias bound that is sharp for the MT functional and vanishes for remote outliers, and give a globally convergent linearized ADMM with closed-form updates.

papers.title: Almost entropic matroids and $(k,L)$-systems
papers.abstract: For an integer $k$ and a set of integers $L$, a $(k,L)$-system is a family of $k$-element sets such that the size of the intersection of any two distinct members belongs to $L$. Let $m(n,k,L)$ denote the maximum size of a $(k,L)$-system on a ground set of $n$ elements. In this work, we establish a close connection between the asymptotic growth of $m(n,k,L)$ and almost entropic matroids. As a consequence, we obtain a general computable upper bound on the asymptotics of $m(n,k,L)$ that unifies and strengthens all previously known upper bounds.

papers.title: On the MDS conjecture in even characteristic
papers.abstract: We prove that every nontrivial linear $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) code over a finite field $\F_q$ of characteristic two satisfies $n\le q+1$, except in dimensions $k=3$ and $k=q-1$, where $n\le q+2$. This resolves the linear MDS conjecture in even characteristic.

papers.title: Timing and Reliability Limits of Position-Assisted UWB Multicast Audio
papers.abstract: One-to-many ultra-wideband (UWB) transport can disseminate shared audio blocks without replicating a downlink stream for every receiver. Yet common reception does not ensure aligned electrical playback, coincident acoustic arrival, or delivery to an entire receiver group. This paper develops a unified feasibility analysis of position-assisted UWB multicast audio that separates clock and actuation error, age-dependent acoustic propagation compensation, correlated block erasures, and reserved communication resources. We derive a conditional bound on one-listener arrival spread, a stationary expression for all-receiver block delivery under common and receiver-local losses, and complementary bounds for reliability-constrained admission. Reproducible Monte Carlo experiments examine 4,590 policy--run records across clock, localization, channel, and slot configurations. For eight receivers, affine clock correction produces a mean run-level 95th-percentile electronic span of $21.19\us$, while position assistance reduces the corresponding one-listener acoustic arrival span from $21.95\ms$ to $419.43\us$. Under the stated $30\us$ timing criterion, 98.86\% of compensated events still exceed the threshold. For 64 receivers, three block copies attain an all-receiver delivery probability of approximately 0.97478 under the modeled correlated channel. The analysis exposes the distinct failure mechanisms of position age, shared fades, retransmission limits, and schedule saturation, and establishes joint criteria for interpreting synchronous multicast audio performance.

papers.title: Beamfocusing Versus Airy Beams: Does Antenna Blockage Require Beam Bending?
papers.abstract: Airy beams are often proposed in array beamforming to bend beams around obstacles. We prove that, for a single-antenna receiver, conventional beamfocusing maximizes the received power regardless of how many antennas are blocked and, in expectation, even with phase errors in the channel state information. This also holds for multi-antenna receivers under a phase-separability condition that is satisfied in rank-one channels. Numerical results confirm that unmodified beamfocusing is optimal for physically small receivers (i.e., those that fit within the beamwidth) when an obstacle is present. For physically larger receivers, the optimal precoding deviates from beamfocusing to better illuminate the receiver's unobstructed parts, but will not become Airy beams. While Airy beams can be configured to perform well, their ability to follow a bent trajectory in front of an obstacle does not maximize the received power behind it.

papers.title: Four Function Theorems Through Optimal Transport and Entropic Analogs
papers.abstract: We study entropic versions of four-function inequalities and give transport proofs of the Euclidean Ahlswede-Daykin theorem and a four-function version of the Prekopa-Leindler inequality due to Cordero-Erausquin and Maurey. One of our main results shows that the sharp range for the four-function inequality for equally weighted power means of finite orders \(\alpha,\beta\) is \(0\leq\alpha+\beta\leq2\), with the Ahlswede-Daykin min-max inequality obtained as a limit. En route, we prove corresponding entropy inequalities under the quadratic optimal transport coupling, including an entropy power inequality for the minimum and maximum in Euclidean space. We also study the stability of four-function inequalities under convolution with log-concave product densities, recovering the preservation of log-supermodularity established by Karlin and Rinott, and explain its application to a conditional entropy power inequality for log-supermodular random variables.

papers.title: Non-Stationarity Breaks Permutation Surrogates in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Diagnosis and Remedies
papers.abstract: Reporting guidance for information-theoretic measures is rarely tested against ground truth. We test one guardrail in two multi-agent reinforcement learning games, a social dilemma and a coordination race, where directed influence between selected agent pairs is zero by construction, over 100 seeds. Omitting one precondition, exclusion of the non-stationary training transient, gives false-positive rates of 100.00% and 99.95%: agents annealing exploration independently, in runs that never met, are flagged as influencing one another. Excluding the transient reaches 3.05% in the social dilemma but 11.8% in the coordination game, so the non-stationarity must be treated and exclusion is neither the only way nor sufficient. What we recommend instead changes the null model. Series, statistic and estimand are left untouched: permuting the source within blocks of training time reaches 5.25% and 5.50%, the only one of the three at or below the size of the test in both games. The construction is not new, being a restricted permutation local to blocks of training time; the measurement is. A third null control, four learners in the social dilemma, defeats all three, and there conditioning costs three times what ours does, 15.20 points against 4.55. Titrating injected links separates it from conditioning on identical pairs, 82.5% against 58.0%, while the ablated test reports a positive with or without a link, so its apparent sensitivity is uninformative. Five block counts spanning 16 to 256 land in the nominal region. Code and data are released.
